title: Viewport breakpoint harmonization for Billing & Rollouts dashboards
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Problem: Multiple console pages (Billing/Cost Overview, Rollouts, and associated dashboards) render inconsistently across viewport sizes and browsers. Symptoms include: table columns overflowing at tablet widths, charts clipping axis labels in Firefox, modals causing page jumps on iOS Safari, and inconsistent sticky filter behavior across Chrome and Edge. Goal: Create a harmonized breakpoint system and component-level rules so tables, charts, and modals behave predictably from 320px to 2560px and across Chrome, Firefox, Safari (iOS and macOS), and Edge. Deliverables: prototyped responsive rules, updated component spec sheets, dev-ready tokens and interactions, and QA checklist for cross-browser validation.
acceptance_criteria: All affected pages use a shared breakpoint map and documented component behaviors
Tables gracefully collapse and enable horizontal scroll only when a defined minimum column set is present
Charts preserve axis labels without overlap down to 360px by switching to abbreviated ticks and condensed legends
Modals use a consistent stacking and scroll-lock strategy that prevents background jumps on iOS Safari
Sticky filter/toolbars remain pinned but never cover critical controls on small viewports
Cross-browser QA passes on latest stable Chrome, Firefox, Safari (iOS + macOS), and Edge with screenshots recorded

notes: Unique aspects: unify responsive behavior across feature areas (billing, rollouts, dashboards) rather than per-page hacks
Risk: aggressive column collapse may hide billing line-items that finance teams expect — mitigate via explicit 'expand' affordance and analytics telemetry on collapse
Design token approach preferred over per-component breakpoints to make runtime overrides easier for Dedicated/Private deployments
